description: Claims verified against source excerpts; JEV Noul is triage, manual notes override only the listed borderline cases.

claims.claim: AWS App Runner is no longer open to new customers.
claims.excerpt: AWS App Runner is no longer open to new customers. Existing AWS App Runner customers can continue to use the service as normal.

claims.claim: AWS recommends Amazon ECS Express Mode as the migration path from App Runner.
claims.excerpt: We recommend that customers explore Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Express Mode when migrating from AWS App Runner.

claims.claim: Amazon ECS Express Mode has no additional charge; users pay only for the underlying AWS resources.
claims.excerpt: ECS Express Mode is available in all AWS Regions at no additional charge, and users pay only for the AWS resources used to run their applications.

claims.claim: A Fargate task targets Graviton by setting the CPU architecture to ARM64 in the ECS task definition.
claims.excerpt: You can simply specify the CPU Architecture as Arm64 in your Amazon ECS Task Definition to target AWS Fargate powered by Arm-based AWS Graviton Processors.

claims.claim: Fargate on Graviton2 was announced with up to 40% better price-performance and 20% lower cost than x86 Fargate (2021 launch claim).
claims.excerpt: AWS Fargate powered by AWS Graviton2 processors delivers up to 40 percent better price-performance at 20 percent lower cost over comparable Intel x86-based Fargate for containerized applications.

claims.claim: AWS Graviton4-based R8g instances deliver up to 30% better performance than Graviton3-based R7g instances.
claims.excerpt: AWS Graviton4-based Amazon EC2 R8g instances deliver up to 30% better performance than AWS Graviton3-based Amazon EC2 R7g instances.

claims.claim: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2, Fargate and Lambda usage.
claims.excerpt: These plans automatically apply to EC2 instance usage regardless of instance family, size, AZ, Region, OS or tenancy, and also apply to Fargate or Lambda usage.

claims.claim: Compute Savings Plans can reduce costs by up to 66%.
claims.excerpt: Compute Savings Plans provide the most flexibility and help to reduce your costs by up to 66%.

claims.claim: Aurora Serverless v2 can pause automatically when minimum capacity is set to 0 ACUs.
claims.excerpt: The automatic pause is enabled by setting the minimum capacity of 0 ACUs and is configurable at the cluster level.

claims.claim: Setting Aurora Serverless v2 minimum capacity to 0.5 ACU or more disables automatic pause.
claims.excerpt: Setting the minimum capacity to 0.5 or greater disables the automatic pause feature

claims.claim: The Aurora Serverless v2 auto-pause inactivity period can be set between 300 seconds and 86,400 seconds.
claims.excerpt: You can specify between 300 seconds (5 minutes) and 86,400 seconds (24 hours) for the delay period with no database traffic before pause is initiated.

claims.claim: Aurora Serverless v2 auto-pause requires a minimum capacity of 2 ACUs.
claims.excerpt: The automatic pause is enabled by setting the minimum capacity of 0 ACUs and is configurable at the cluster level.

claims.claim: OpenSearch Serverless minimum OCU can be set to 0 per collection group, so no OCUs are needed when idle.
claims.excerpt: You can set a minimum and maximum OCU per collection group, separately for indexing and searching. When not actively indexing or searching, OCUs scale down to the minimum OCU value independently for indexing and search. If the minimum is set to 0, no OCUs are needed when idle.

claims.claim: At general availability, the first OpenSearch Serverless collection in an account provisioned 4 OCUs even without activity.
claims.excerpt: When you create the first collection endpoint in an account, OpenSearch Serverless provisions 4 OCUs (2 ingest that include primary and standby, and 2 search that include two copies for high availability). These OCUs are instantiated even though there is no activity on the serverless endpoint to avoid any cold start latencies.
claims.manual_note: JEV p=0.62 (uncertain). Manual check: the 2023 GA blog states 4 OCUs and the no-activity instantiation verbatim. The claim is historical and must not be read as current OpenSearch Serverless behavior.

claims.claim: AWS recommends three dedicated master nodes for each production OpenSearch Service domain.
claims.excerpt: We recommend that you use Multi-AZ with Standby, which adds three dedicated master nodes to each production OpenSearch Service domain.

claims.claim: AWS recommends two dedicated master nodes for production OpenSearch Service domains.
claims.excerpt: We recommend that you use Multi-AZ with Standby, which adds three dedicated master nodes to each production OpenSearch Service domain. Never choose an even number of dedicated master nodes.

claims.claim: Amazon S3 Vectors is generally available and reduces vector storage costs by up to 90% (vendor claim).
claims.excerpt: Amazon S3 Vectors, a new cloud object storage service with native vector support, is now generally available. It delivers cost-optimized vector storage for AI applications, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), semantic search, and inference at a billion-vector scale. S3 Vectors offers elasticity, durability, and availability similar to Amazon S3, reducing vector storage costs by up to 90%.

claims.claim: S3 Vectors supports SSE-KMS with customer-managed keys.
claims.excerpt: S3 Vectors supports server-side encryption using S3-managed keys (SSE-S3) or AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) for customer-managed keys.

claims.claim: S3 Vectors is recommended when sub-10 millisecond query latency is required.
claims.excerpt: It's recommended when latency can be approximately 100 ms or more, or for fast-growing vector datasets at moderate QPS.

claims.claim: An interface VPC endpoint is billed hourly for each Availability Zone where it is provisioned, even if idle.
claims.excerpt: There is an hourly charge for each VPC endpoint provisioned in each Availability Zone, regardless of the state of its association with the service.

claims.claim: Interface VPC endpoints charge data processing per GB processed.
claims.excerpt: Data processing charges apply for each GB processed through the VPC endpoint, regardless of the traffic's source or destination.

claims.claim: VPC gateway endpoints for S3 have no charge.
claims.excerpt: VPC gateway endpoints (S3) | No charge | No charge

claims.claim: A NAT gateway is charged for each hour it is available and for each GB it processes.
claims.excerpt: When you provision a NAT gateway, you are charged for each hour that your NAT gateway is available and each gigabyte of data that it processes.

claims.claim: CloudFront Price Class 100 does not include South America edge locations.
claims.excerpt: | Price Class 100 | Yes | Yes | **x** | **x** | **x** | **x** | **x** | **x** |  (columns: United States, Mexico, and Canada | Europe, Israel, and Türkiye | South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, Egypt, and Middle East | South America | ...)

claims.claim: CloudFront Price Class 200 includes South America edge locations.
claims.excerpt: | Price Class 200 | Yes | Yes | Yes | **x** | Yes | **x** | Yes | Yes |  (columns: United States, Mexico, and Canada | Europe, Israel, and Türkiye | South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, Egypt, and Middle East | South America | ...)

claims.claim: CloudFront Price Class All includes South America edge locations.
claims.excerpt: | Price Class All | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |  (columns: ... | South America | ...)

claims.claim: GitHub Actions can exchange its OIDC token for temporary AWS credentials, without long-term access keys.
claims.excerpt: Use the OpenID Connect (OIDC) standard to federate GitHub Actions identity through IAM. ... exchange the GitHub token for temporary AWS credentials without needing long-term access keys.

claims.claim: IAM rejects a GitHub OIDC trust policy that does not restrict the token sub claim.
claims.excerpt: IAM rejects a GitHub OIDC trust policy that doesn't restrict `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` (or `job_workflow_ref`).

claims.claim: The CloudWatch OTLP metrics endpoint accepts bearer token authentication.
claims.excerpt: CloudWatch OTLP endpoints support bearer token auth for metrics and logs.

claims.claim: The X-Ray OTLP traces endpoint accepts bearer token authentication.
claims.excerpt: | **Traces** | `https://xray.region.amazonaws.com/v1/traces` | `[Bearer token auth not supported, hence excluded from this blog post]` |

claims.claim: SageMaker asynchronous inference can autoscale the instance count to zero when there are no requests.
claims.excerpt: Asynchronous Inference enables you to save on costs by autoscaling the instance count to zero when there are no requests to process, so you only pay when your endpoint is processing requests.

claims.claim: SageMaker managed spot training can optimize training cost by up to 90% over on-demand instances.
claims.excerpt: Managed spot training can optimize the cost of training models up to 90% over on-demand instances.

claims.claim: Managed spot training needs no checkpointing for any training job length.
claims.excerpt: Unless your training job will complete quickly, we recommend you use checkpointing with managed spot training.

claims.claim: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is based on six pillars, including Sustainability.
claims.excerpt: The framework is based on six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability

claims.claim: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is based on five pillars.
claims.excerpt: The framework is based on six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability

claims.claim: Graviton4 is the latest Graviton generation according to the containers guide consulted on 2026-11-14.
claims.excerpt: AWS has launched three additional generations including the latest: Graviton4.

claims.claim: The Azure Well-Architected Framework has five pillars: Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence and Performance Efficiency.
claims.excerpt: Pillars. Reliability: Ensures that the workload meets the uptime and recovery targets by building redundancy and resiliency at scale. Security: Protect the workload from attacks by maintaining confidentiality and data integrity. Cost Optimization: Adopt an optimization mindset at organizational, architectural, and tactical levels. Operational Excellence: Reduce issues in production by building holistic observability and automated systems. Performance Efficiency: Adjust to changes in demands placed on the workload through horizontal scaling and testing changes before deploying to production.

claims.claim: Sustainability is one of the five pillars of the Azure Well-Architected Framework.
claims.excerpt: Pillars: Reliability; Security; Cost Optimization; Operational Excellence; Performance Efficiency. (Sustainability appears among the workloads, not the pillars.)

claims.claim: Most Azure Container Apps applications can scale to zero.
claims.excerpt: Autoscale your apps based on any KEDA-supported scale trigger. Most applications can scale to zero. Applications that scale on CPU or memory load can't scale to zero.

claims.claim: Azure Container Apps applications that scale on CPU or memory load cannot scale to zero.
claims.excerpt: Applications that scale on CPU or memory load can't scale to zero.

claims.claim: Azure Container Apps applications that scale on CPU load scale to zero when idle.
claims.excerpt: Applications that scale on CPU or memory load can't scale to zero.

claims.claim: Azure Container Apps supports internal ingress for internal-only endpoints.
claims.excerpt: Use internal ingress and service discovery for secure internal-only endpoints with built-in DNS-based service discovery.

claims.claim: Zone-redundant high availability for PostgreSQL flexible server replicates changes synchronously to a warm standby with zero data loss.
claims.excerpt: If you configure zone redundant high availability, the service provisions and maintains a warm standby server across the availability zone within the same Azure region. The data changes on the source server are synchronously replicated to the standby server to ensure zero data loss.

claims.claim: In Brazil South, new zone-redundant HA deployments of PostgreSQL flexible server are temporarily blocked.
claims.excerpt: | Brazil South | ✅ (v3/v4/v5) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ $ | ✅ | ❌ |  Legend: $ indicates new zone-redundant high availability deployments are temporarily blocked in these regions.

claims.claim: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server supports geo-redundant backup in Brazil South.
claims.excerpt: | Brazil South | ✅ (v3/v4/v5) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ $ | ✅ | ❌ |  (columns: Intel Compute | AMD Compute | Confidential Compute | Zone-Redundant HA | Same-Zone HA | Geo-Redundant backup)

claims.claim: Stopping an Azure PostgreSQL flexible server stops compute billing immediately; the server stays stopped for seven days unless restarted.
claims.excerpt: The compute tier billing stops immediately when you stop the server. ... The server remains stopped for seven days unless you restart it sooner.

claims.claim: With virtual network integration, Azure PostgreSQL flexible server denies public access.
claims.excerpt: With virtual network integration, public access is denied, and servers can't be reached by using public endpoints.

claims.claim: Azure PostgreSQL flexible server backup retention defaults to seven days and can be set up to 35 days.
claims.excerpt: The default backup retention period is seven days. You can optionally configure the retention for up to 35 days.

claims.claim: Azure AI Search hybrid search runs full-text and vector queries in parallel and merges results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
claims.excerpt: Runs full-text search and vector search in parallel. Merges results from each query by using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).

claims.claim: Azure AI Search hybrid search merges full-text and vector results by averaging their raw scores.
claims.excerpt: Merges results from each query by using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). An RRF algorithm merges the results.

claims.claim: Azure Blob immutable storage supports time-based retention policies and legal holds in a WORM state.
claims.excerpt: Immutable storage for Azure Blob Storage lets you store business-critical data in a WORM (Write Once, Read Many) state ... Time-based retention policies ... Legal hold policies

claims.claim: A locked time-based retention policy on Azure Blob storage can be deleted by the account owner.
claims.excerpt: You can't delete a locked time-based retention policy. You can extend the retention period, but you can't decrease it.

claims.claim: Azure Blob immutable storage has no extra capacity charge.
claims.excerpt: There's no extra capacity charge for using immutable storage. Immutable data is priced in the same way as mutable data.

claims.claim: Version-level WORM on Azure Blob requires versioning to be enabled on the account.
claims.excerpt: Version-level WORM policy: Configure a time-based retention policy at the account, container, or version level (versioning must be enabled on the account).

claims.claim: Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoints charge only for compute and networking, with no added surcharge.
claims.excerpt: When you use a managed online endpoint, you pay for the compute and networking charges. There's no added surcharge.

claims.claim: Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoints scale to zero instances when idle.
claims.excerpt: When you use a managed online endpoint, you pay for the compute and networking charges. There's no added surcharge.

claims.claim: For Java applications, Azure Monitor recommends the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro for Java.
claims.excerpt: For most code-based server-side scenarios, use the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro for .NET, Node.js, and Python, or the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro for Java.

claims.claim: Azure Artifact Signing (formerly Trusted Signing) is generally available.
claims.excerpt: Trusted Signing is now Artifact Signing—and it's officially Generally Available!

claims.claim: Azure Artifact Signing public-trust certificates are available to individual developers located in Brazil.
claims.excerpt: Public Trust certificates are available to organizations in the United States, Canada, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, and Israel. Individual developers must be located in the United States or Canada.

claims.claim: Azure Artifact Signing Basic plan costs 9.99 USD per month for up to 5,000 signatures.
claims.excerpt: Basic Plan: $9.99/month for up to 5,000 signatures; $0.005 per additional signature.
claims.manual_note: JEV p=0.68 (uncertain). Manual check: the Azure product page states 'Basic Plan: $9.99/month for up to 5,000 signatures'. The Azure Retail Prices convention is USD, so the $ sign is USD.

claims.claim: The Azure Retail Prices API provides an unauthenticated experience to retrieve retail rates.
claims.excerpt: This API gives you an unauthenticated experience to get retail rates for all Azure services.

claims.claim: The Azure Retail Prices API returns a maximum of 1,000 records per request and provides NextPageLink pagination.
claims.excerpt: For each API request, a maximum of 1,000 records are returned. At the end of the API response, it has the link to next page.

claims.claim: The Azure MCP Server is developed in the microsoft/mcp repository, and the Azure/azure-mcp repository was archived on August 25, 2025.
claims.excerpt: This repository is archived as of August 25, 2025. Going forward, the Azure MCP team is using https://github.com/microsoft/mcp to develop the code and issues formerly in this repository.
